summary: 429s observed after signed URL refresh and HTTP/2 proxy pool rotation during concurrent bulk-embed ingest
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart is seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses when running concurrent bulk embedding uploads (500+ parallel workers). The spike correlates with the customers' signed URL refresh job and with the edge HTTP/2 proxy rotating connections/pools.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests in affected windows return 429; ingest backfill jobs fail/retry and extend pipeline time.
- Customer reports elevated error rates for 2–10 minute windows during their scheduled token refresh job.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (BrightCart tenant) in us-west
- Client: internal orchestrator using HTTP/2 multiplexed connections across a small proxy pool
- Model: embedding-asmall-v1 (batch size 128)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start bulk-embed job with 500 concurrent workers using signed URLs refreshed every 30 minutes.
2) During refresh window, workers re-request signed URLs and immediately re-use existing long-lived HTTP/2 connections that are pinned to proxy pool members.
3) Observe 429s from Redwood API and sporadic retry storms on client side.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include typical rate-limit headers (x-ratelimit-remaining: 0, x-ratelimit-reset: short window) for otherwise healthy tenants.
- Logs show same API key associated with multiple concurrent connection IDs and repeated token-checks (possible double-counting).
- Proxy pool rotation events (connection close/rebind) line up with first 429 in the window.

Expected behavior:
- Signed URL refresh should not create double-counting of tokens across connection churn. Client retries should see coherent rate-limit headers and successful backoff recovery.

Customer-provided logs (redacted):
- 2026-03-12T09:02:11Z INFO worker-233 request /v1/embeds 200 tokens=384
- 2026-03-12T09:02:18Z INFO auth refresh signed-url tenant=brightcart
- 2026-03-12T09:02:19Z WARN proxy pool rotate host=egw-5c3 conn=0x7f4c
- 2026-03-12T09:02:20Z ERROR request /v1/embeds 429 x-ratelimit-remaining=0 x-ratelimit-reset=13
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by support (Maya): reproduced at lower concurrency (50 workers) in staging when forcing signed-url rotation + connection pin churn. Observed duplicated accounting events in rate-limiter logs where the same ephemeral token fingerprint was recorded twice across two connection IDs. Hypothesis: when signed URLs refresh and clients reconnect/rebind via HTTP/2 proxy pool, token/session dedupe logic misses in-flight rebinds and increments bucket twice.

What we checked:
- Edge-proxy logs (proxy nodes egp-5c3, egp-5c4) for connection reuse and stream resets.
- Rate-limiter audit trail for token fingerprinting and per-connection accounting.
- Ingest orchestrator retry patterns and backoff timing from customer.
- Related config: their signed-url TTL = 180s, refresh job overlaps with TTL expiry and immediately issues new signed URLs while maintaining connection reuse.

Intermediate findings:
- Rebind path in edge-proxy emits a connection-rebind event but does not surface to the rate-limiter's dedupe hook in ~10% of churns (race condition).
- When dedupe hook misses, both the old and new connection get charged for the same logical token for a short window, reducing available tokens and triggering 429s.
- Reproduced correlation locally; created minimal repro and log trace (see linked PR/trace).
resolution_notes:
Workaround provided to customer (2026-03-13):
- Short-term: stagger signed URL refreshes across worker fleets and increase TTL to 10 minutes to avoid tight refresh windows. Reduce parallelism during known refresh windows.
- Medium-term: we will enable a feature-flagged fix in edge-proxy that ensures the rebind path calls the rate-limiter dedupe hook synchronously. Patch PR created (see related_github_prs).
- Follow-up: schedule an ops rollout during low-traffic window (proposed 2026-03-20) and monitor rate-limit metrics for BrightCart.

Post-fix verification plan:
- Canary the fix on 2 proxy nodes in us-west for BrightCart tenant.
- Run customer's reproducible load (500 workers) at +10% for 30 minutes and assert that 429s do not exceed historical baseline.
- Rollout and monitor for 48 hours.

2026-03-13 — Ethan Cole (SRE): Reproduced lower-concurrency repro in staging. Noted duplicate accounting trace. Linked PR to patch the rebind dedupe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/512
2026-03-13 — Support (Maya): Shared workaround (stagger refresh, increase TTL) and asked customer to coordinate a load window for verification.
2026-03-14 — Customer: Applied staggered refresh and reported immediate drop in 429 incidence to <1% during next run. Agreed to proceed with canary once patch is available.
